question.text: GST applies to commodity derivative transactions on:

answer.text: The billed amount at the Final Settlement Price on physical delivery, plus brokerage and exchange trading/clearing fees
The entire notional contract value on every trade
Only the profit earned from trading
No GST applies to commodity derivatives

explanation.text: The Logic: For commodity derivatives, GST is levied on the billed amount at the Final Settlement Price when a contract results in physical delivery, and is also levied on brokerage and on exchange trading and clearing fees as services. The Trap: GST is not charged on every trade's full notional contract value, nor only on trading profits, and it is not exempt for commodity derivatives. Leaving out the delivery-side GST on the FSP-billed amount is the common omission. Note: When totalling all-in trading cost, factor in CTT, stamp duty and GST on brokerage and exchange charges, and add delivery-side GST on FSP when physical delivery occurs.
